source_evidence: This fee subtracts a set percentage from any gain in the index. These features can reduce your return in the same way that a direct fee would even if the annuity is called a “no fee” annuity.
question: Misconception: If an indexed annuity is advertised as having “no fees,” a spread cannot reduce the return credited to the account. Is that true?
answer: No. A spread subtracts a set percentage from an index gain, so it can reduce the return even when it is not presented as a direct fee. For example, with a 9% index return and a 3% spread, the credited return would be 6%.
